claim: Csk is the primary negative regulator of Src-family kinases (SFK).
source: The C-terminal Src kinase (Csk), the primary negative regulator of Src-family kinases (SFK), plays a crucial role in controlling basal and inducible receptor signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about Csk's role.

claim: Csk plays a crucial role in controlling basal and inducible receptor signaling.
source: The C-terminal Src kinase (Csk), the primary negative regulator of Src-family kinases (SFK), plays a crucial role in controlling basal and inducible receptor signaling.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the abstract.

claim: Inhibition of CskAS during TCR stimulation led to stronger and more prolonged TCR signaling.
source: Inhibition of CskAS during TCR stimulation led to stronger and more prolonged TCR signaling and to increased proliferation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in the figures.

claim: Inhibition of CskAS during TCR stimulation led to increased proliferation.
source: Inhibition of CskAS during TCR stimulation led to stronger and more prolonged TCR signaling and to increased proliferation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: Inhibition of CskAS enhanced activation by weak but strictly cognate agonists.
source: Inhibition of CskAS enhanced activation by weak but strictly cognate agonists.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: A very small increase in SFK activity was sufficient to potentiate T cell responses to weak agonists.
source: Titration of Csk inhibition revealed that a very small increase in SFK activity was sufficient to potentiate T cell responses to weak agonists.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Csk plays an important role in setting the TCR signaling threshold.
source: Csk plays an important role, not only in basal signaling, but also in setting the TCR signaling threshold and affinity recognition.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Csk plays an important role in affinity recognition.
source: Csk plays an important role, not only in basal signaling, but also in setting the TCR signaling threshold and affinity recognition.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: SFKs are ubiquitous regulators of basal and inducible receptor signaling.
source: SFKs are ubiquitous regulators of basal and inducible receptor signaling.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The seven SFK family members are expressed in various combinations in different cell types.
source: The seven family members are expressed in various combinations in different cell types, have unique substrate specificity and are differentially regulated by phosphatases and localization (Lowell, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lowell, 2004.

claim: SFK family members have unique substrate specificity.
source: The seven family members are expressed in various combinations in different cell types, have unique substrate specificity and are differentially regulated by phosphatases and localization (Lowell, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lowell, 2004.

claim: SFK family members are differentially regulated by phosphatases and localization.
source: The seven family members are expressed in various combinations in different cell types, have unique substrate specificity and are differentially regulated by phosphatases and localization (Lowell, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lowell, 2004.

claim: All SFK family members share a common negative regulator Csk.
source: However, they share a common negative regulator Csk.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The strength and duration of TCR signaling in response to antigen stimulation dictates the magnitude and quality of primary and secondary immune responses.
source: In T cells, the strength and duration of T cell antigen receptor (TCR) signaling in response to antigen stimulation dictates the magnitude and quality of primary and secondary immune responses (Smith-Garvin et al., 2009; Chakraborty and Weiss, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Smith-Garvin et al., 2009 and Chakraborty and Weiss, 2014.

claim: Lck regulates TCR signaling by phosphorylating tyrosines in the cytoplasmic segments of the TCR ζ and CD3 chains.
source: The SFK Lck regulates TCR signaling by phosphorylating tyrosines in the cytoplasmic segments of the TCR ζ and CD3 chains, basally and during antigen recognition, as well as by phosphorylating downstream kinases such as ZAP-70 and ITK (Chan et al., 1995; Heyeck et al., 1997; Smith-Garvin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chan et al., 1995; Heyeck et al., 1997; Smith-Garvin et al., 2009.

claim: Lck phosphorylates downstream kinases such as ZAP-70 and ITK.
source: The SFK Lck regulates TCR signaling by phosphorylating tyrosines in the cytoplasmic segments of the TCR ζ and CD3 chains, basally and during antigen recognition, as well as by phosphorylating downstream kinases such as ZAP-70 and ITK (Chan et al., 1995; Heyeck et al., 1997; Smith-Garvin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chan et al., 1995; Heyeck et al., 1997; Smith-Garvin et al., 2009.

claim: The availability and recruitment of active Lck has been proposed to be the rate-limiting step in discriminating agonist affinity.
source: The availability and recruitment of active Lck has been proposed to be the rate-limiting step in discriminating agonist affinity (Stepanek et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stepanek et al., 2014.

claim: Weak agonists with shorter half-lives of pMHC-TCR interaction have less time to recruit active CD4 or CD8 co-receptor bound Lck.
source: Weak agonists with shorter half-lives of pMHC (peptide-bound major histocompatibility complex)-TCR interaction have less time to recruit active CD4 or CD8 co-receptor bound Lck.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the kinetic proofreading model.

claim: Active Lck (phosphorylated on Y394) is critical for downstream signaling.
source: Active Lck (phosphorylated on Y394) is critical for downstream signaling and can be detected in the basal state, but its level does not change appreciably after TCR stimulation (Nika et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nika et al., 2010.

claim: Active Lck can be detected in the basal state.
source: Active Lck (phosphorylated on Y394) is critical for downstream signaling and can be detected in the basal state, but its level does not change appreciably after TCR stimulation (Nika et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nika et al., 2010.

claim: The level of active Lck does not change appreciably after TCR stimulation.
source: Active Lck (phosphorylated on Y394) is critical for downstream signaling and can be detected in the basal state, but its level does not change appreciably after TCR stimulation (Nika et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nika et al., 2010.

claim: Lck is tightly regulated by phosphorylation on two conserved tyrosines.
source: Lck is tightly regulated by phosphorylation on two conserved tyrosines.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Trans-autophosphorylation of Lck's kinase domain activation loop tyrosine Y394 increases its catalytic activity.
source: Trans-autophosphorylation of its kinase domain activation loop tyrosine, Y394, increases its catalytic activity, whereas phosphorylation of its C-terminal tail inhibitory tyrosine, Y505, promotes its closed, inactive conformation (Palacios and Weiss, 2004; Chakraborty and Weiss, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Palacios and Weiss, 2004 and Chakraborty and Weiss, 2014.

claim: Phosphorylation of Lck's C-terminal tail inhibitory tyrosine Y505 promotes its closed, inactive conformation.
source: Trans-autophosphorylation of its kinase domain activation loop tyrosine, Y394, increases its catalytic activity, whereas phosphorylation of its C-terminal tail inhibitory tyrosine, Y505, promotes its closed, inactive conformation (Palacios and Weiss, 2004; Chakraborty and Weiss, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Palacios and Weiss, 2004 and Chakraborty and Weiss, 2014.

claim: CD45 regulates Lck activity positively and negatively by dephosphorylating its inhibitory tyrosine and activation loop tyrosine.
source: In T cells, the receptor-like protein tyrosine phosphatase CD45 regulates Lck activity positively and negatively by dephosphorylating its inhibitory tyrosine and activation loop tyrosine (McNeill et al., 2007; Zikherman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to McNeill et al., 2007 and Zikherman et al., 2010.

claim: The major negative regulator of Lck is Csk, which phosphorylates its inhibitory tail tyrosine.
source: However, the major negative regulator of Lck is Csk, which phosphorylates its inhibitory tail tyrosine (Bergman et al., 1992; Levinson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bergman et al., 1992 and Levinson et al., 2008.

claim: Csk is a cytoplasmic protein.
source: Csk is a cytoplasmic protein, yet its predominant role is to phosphorylate the inhibitory tyrosine of SFKs that are localized to membranes (Bergman et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bergman et al., 1992.

claim: Csk's predominant role is to phosphorylate the inhibitory tyrosine of SFKs that are localized to membranes.
source: Csk is a cytoplasmic protein, yet its predominant role is to phosphorylate the inhibitory tyrosine of SFKs that are localized to membranes (Bergman et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bergman et al., 1992.

claim: The association of Csk with PAG in biochemically defined lipid rafts has been observed to diminish in response to TCR stimulation.
source: The association of Csk with PAG in biochemically defined lipid rafts has been observed to diminish in response to TCR stimulation, leading to its proposed involvement in regulating TCR signaling (Torgersen et al., 2001; Davidson et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Torgersen et al., 2001 and Davidson et al., 2003.

claim: Csk returns to lipid raft fractions upon signal termination.
source: Since Csk returns to these fractions upon signal termination, it has also been implicated in the down-regulation of signaling (Torgersen et al., 2001; Davidson et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Torgersen et al., 2001 and Davidson et al., 2003.

claim: Individual genetic deficiencies in PAG, LIME or Dok1/2 have had little effect on TCR signaling and on T cell function.
source: However individual genetic deficiencies in PAG, LIME or Dok1/2 have had little effect on TCR signaling and on T cell function (Brdickova et al., 2003; Dobenecker et al., 2005; Xu et al., 2005; Yasuda et al., 2007), indicating that our understanding of Csk regulation during TCR signal initiation, propagation and termination remains incomplete.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brdickova et al., 2003; Dobenecker et al., 2005; Xu et al., 2005; Yasuda et al., 2007.

claim: Germline deletion of Csk leads to embryonic lethality.
source: Germline deletion of Csk leads to embryonic lethality (Imamoto and Soriano, 1993; Nada et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Imamoto and Soriano, 1993 and Nada et al., 1993.

claim: Conditional deletion of Csk in the T lineage leads to TCR-MHC-independent, but Lck-dependent, passage through both thymic beta selection and positive selection checkpoints.
source: Conditional deletion of Csk in the T lineage leads to TCR-MHC-independent, but Lck-dependent, passage through both thymic beta selection and positive selection checkpoints, both of which require perception of pre-TCR or TCR signaling, respectively (Schmedt and Tarakhovsky, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Schmedt and Tarakhovsky, 2001.

claim: BAC transgenic mice were generated that express a mutant of Csk (CskAS) in the absence of endogenous Csk.
source: We recently generated BAC transgenic mice that express a mutant of Csk (CskAS) in the absence of endogenous Csk (Tan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tan et al., 2014.

claim: CskAS kinase activity can be specifically and rapidly inhibited by 3-iodo-benzyl-PP1 (3-IB-PP1).
source: CskAS kinase activity can be specifically and rapidly inhibited by an analog of the general kinase inhibitor PP1, 3-iodo-benzyl-PP1 (3-IB-PP1).
evidence: This is stated as a property of the CskAS system.

claim: The combined actions of CD45 and Csk establish the basal activity of SFK.
source: Studies in thymocytes in this model system support the notion that the combined actions of CD45 and Csk establish the basal activity of SFK (Tan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tan et al., 2014.

claim: Inhibition of CskAS alone induced strong activation of Lck and Fyn.
source: As previously shown, inhibition of CskAS alone induced strong activation of Lck, as well as Fyn, which was indicated by the hyperphosphorylation of their activation loop tyrosines and the reduced phosphorylation of their inhibitory tyrosines (Tan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tan et al., 2014 and data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Ligation of the TCR alone did not detectably alter Lck phosphorylation.
source: In contrast, ligation of the TCR alone did not detectably alter Lck phosphorylation, consistent with an earlier report (Nika et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nika et al., 2010 and data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Lck activation after CskAS inhibition was associated with only relatively weak downstream phosphorylation of ZAP-70, LAT and PLC-γ1.
source: The striking Lck activation after CskAS inhibition was associated with only relatively weak downstream phosphorylation of ZAP-70, LAT and PLC-γ1 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Downstream signaling was very strongly enhanced when CskAS inhibitor treatment was combined with anti-CD3ε crosslinking.
source: However, this downstream signaling was very strongly enhanced when the CskAS inhibitor treatment was combined with anti-CD3ε crosslinking, as evidenced by the marked increase in ZAP-70, LAT and PLC-γ1 phosphorylation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The magnitude of p-ERK was increased by CskAS inhibition in a 3-IB-PP1 dose-dependent manner.
source: The magnitude of p-ERK was increased by CskAS inhibition in a 3-IB-PP1 dose-dependent manner, with the greatest enhancement seen when using a low dose of anti-CD3ε (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CskAS inhibition alone induced only a small amount of protein phosphorylation downstream of ZAP-70.
source: Notably, CskAS inhibition alone induced only a small amount of protein phosphorylation downstream of ZAP-70 (i.e., LAT and ERK1/2), likely due to spurious activation of a few cells (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1A and 1B.

claim: CskAS inhibition synergized with TCR stimulation leading to downstream signaling.
source: Instead, CskAS inhibition synergized with TCR stimulation leading to downstream signaling.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1A and 1B.

claim: Csk activity plays a crucial role in establishing the TCR activation threshold.
source: Our data strongly suggest that Csk activity plays a crucial role in establishing the TCR activation threshold.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: A reduction in Csk activity lowered the threshold for signal activation and increased TCR sensitivity.
source: Specifically, a reduction in Csk activity lowered the threshold for signal activation and increased TCR sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: CskAS inhibition prolonged phosphorylation of ZAP-70, LAT and PLC-γ1.
source: CskAS inhibition prolonged phosphorylation of ZAP-70, LAT and PLC-γ1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There was evidence of 3-IB-PP1 dose-dependent delay in downregulation of p-ERK.
source: There was evidence of 3-IB-PP1 dose-dependent delay in downregulation of p-ERK, with the down-regulation seeming more heterogeneous and, perhaps, asynchronous compared to the digital up-regulation of the response (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Csk inhibition did not prevent eventual signal attenuation over time.
source: However, Csk inhibition did not prevent eventual signal attenuation over time, indicating that Csk has only a partial role in signal termination.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Other negative regulatory mechanisms must contribute to the termination of TCR signaling.
source: Other negative regulatory mechanisms must contribute to the termination of TCR signaling, albeit more slowly in the absence of Csk (Naramura et al., 2002; Rhee and Veillette, 2012).
evidence: This is an inference from the data and supported by citations to Naramura et al., 2002 and Rhee and Veillette, 2012.

claim: Stimulation of CskAS;OTII CD4+ T cells with an agonistic OVA pMHC tetramer during CskAS inhibition resulted in markedly enhanced phosphorylation of ZAP-70, LAT and PLC-γ1.
source: Stimulation of CskAS;OTII CD4+ T cells with an agonistic OVA pMHC tetramer during CskAS inhibition resulted in markedly enhanced phosphorylation of ZAP-70, LAT and PLC-γ1 (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Stimulation of CskAS;OTII CD4+ T cells with OVA pMHC tetramer during CskAS inhibition led to increased and prolonged ERK1/2 phosphorylation.
source: Stimulation of CskAS;OTII CD4+ T cells with an agonistic OVA pMHC tetramer during CskAS inhibition resulted in markedly enhanced phosphorylation of ZAP-70, LAT and PLC-γ1 (Figure 2A) and led to increased and prolonged ERK1/2 phosphorylation (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Findings with the physiologic OVA pMHC TCR ligand parallel those using anti-CD3ε.
source: Thus, our findings with the physiologic OVA pMHC TCR ligand parallel those using anti-CD3ε, confirming that Csk plays an important role in setting the TCR activation threshold and has a partial role in signal termination.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: At low doses, both anti-CD3ε and OVA pMHC tetramer induced greater cellular proliferation when CskAS was inhibited.
source: At low doses, both anti-CD3ε and OVA pMHC tetramer induced greater cellular proliferation when CskAS was inhibited, consistent with the increased magnitude of proximal TCR signaling.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: By controlling Csk activity, the threshold for TCR signaling and resultant responses can be modulated.
source: Therefore, by controlling Csk activity, the threshold for TCR signaling and resultant responses can be modulated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the proliferation data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Titration of 3-IB-PP1 in CskAS CD8+ T cells revealed a maximum threefold to fourfold enhancement of Lck pY394.
source: Titration of 3-IB-PP1 in CskAS CD8+ T cells revealed a maximum threefold to fourfold enhancement of Lck pY394, which correlated with increased Lck activity (Figure 3A) (Chakraborty and Weiss, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and a citation to Chakraborty and Weiss, 2014.

claim: At resting state 25–33% of Lck was phosphorylated at Y394.
source: Thus at resting state 25–33% of Lck was phosphorylated at Y394, which agrees with some previous estimates (Nika et al., 2010) and is higher than others (Ballek et al., 2015).
evidence: This is inferred from the plateau with high drug doses shown in Figure 3A and compared to citations.

claim: Low doses of 3-IB-PP1 (1 μM or less) induced at most a 50% upregulation of pY394.
source: Low doses of 3-IB-PP1 (1 μM or less) induced at most a 50% upregulation of pY394, while doses of 5–10 μM induced a threefold to fourfold upregulation.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Doses of 5–10 μM 3-IB-PP1 induced a threefold to fourfold upregulation of Lck pY394.
source: Low doses of 3-IB-PP1 (1 μM or less) induced at most a 50% upregulation of pY394, while doses of 5–10 μM induced a threefold to fourfold upregulation.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Phosphorylation of the inhibitory tail Y505 did not decrease as appreciably as expected.
source: Surprisingly, phosphorylation of the inhibitory tail Y505, the direct target of Csk, did not decrease as appreciably.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Lck is actively phosphorylated by Csk.
source: This observation suggests that Lck is actively phosphorylated by Csk, but a substantial proportion of pY505 is either inaccessible for dephosphorylation by CD45 or is dephosphorylated over a longer timescale.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that pY505 does not decrease much despite Csk inhibition.

claim: CD4+ and CD8+ T cells have identical responses to Csk inhibition when normalized to their basal level of Lck phosphorylation.
source: However, we found that CD4+ and CD8+ T cells have identical responses to Csk inhibition when normalized to their basal level of Lck phosphorylation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: CD8+ T cells express ∼15% more Lck than CD4+ T cells.
source: Interestingly, CD8+ T cells express ∼15% more Lck (Olszowy et al., 1995) and have a higher (∼20%) basal amount of inhibitory tail pY505 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Olszowy et al., 1995 and data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: CD8+ T cells have a higher (∼20%) basal amount of inhibitory tail pY505 phosphorylation than CD4+ T cells.
source: Interestingly, CD8+ T cells express ∼15% more Lck (Olszowy et al., 1995) and have a higher (∼20%) basal amount of inhibitory tail pY505 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, pY394 increased much more markedly than the associated decrease in pY505 in response to low doses of the Csk inhibitor.
source: In both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, pY394 increased much more markedly than the associated decrease in pY505 in response to low doses of the Csk inhibitor.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Short-term CskAS;OTI CD8+ T cell stimulation with bead-bound OVA-MHC tetramer was enhanced even by low levels of Csk inhibition (<1 μM).
source: Short-term CskAS;OTI CD8+ T cell stimulation with bead-bound OVA-MHC tetramer was enhanced even by low levels of Csk inhibition (<1 μM) (Figure 3B), as demonstrated by the degree of PLC-γ1 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: At low inhibitor dose (<1 μM), Lck pY394 did not increase by more than 50%.
source: At this inhibitor dose, Lck pY394 did not increase by more than 50%, suggesting that even subtle changes in Lck activity can potentiate proximal signaling.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Even subtle changes in Lck activity can potentiate proximal signaling.
source: At this inhibitor dose, Lck pY394 did not increase by more than 50%, suggesting that even subtle changes in Lck activity can potentiate proximal signaling.
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Higher doses of the inhibitor potentiated Lck signaling even further.
source: Higher doses of the inhibitor potentiated Lck signaling even further, suggesting Csk and Lck activity can be titrated over a wide range.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Csk and Lck activity can be titrated over a wide range.
source: Higher doses of the inhibitor potentiated Lck signaling even further, suggesting Csk and Lck activity can be titrated over a wide range.
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Lck is proposed to be the crucial gate-keeper in kinetic proof-reading models that attempt to explain the exquisite affinity discrimination of T cells.
source: Lck not only initiates TCR-dependent signaling but is also proposed to be the crucial gate-keeper in kinetic proof-reading models that attempt to explain the exquisite affinity discrimination of T cells of agonists with only slightly different half-lives (Palmer and Naeher, 2009; Stepanek et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Palmer and Naeher, 2009 and Stepanek et al., 2014.

claim: Strong CskAS inhibition (5 μM) led to marked augmentation of CD69 expression in responses to weak agonists (T4, Q4H7, G4).
source: When CskAS;OTI CD8+ T cells were stimulated by APCs preloaded with peptides of different agonist potency during strong CskAS inhibition (5 μM), we observed marked augmentation of CD69 expression in responses to weak (T4, Q4H7, G4) agonists, contrasting with only slight enhancement of the responses to strong (OVA, Q4R7) agonists (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Strong CskAS inhibition (5 μM) led to only slight enhancement of the responses to strong agonists (OVA, Q4R7).
source: When CskAS;OTI CD8+ T cells were stimulated by APCs preloaded with peptides of different agonist potency during strong CskAS inhibition (5 μM), we observed marked augmentation of CD69 expression in responses to weak (T4, Q4H7, G4) agonists, contrasting with only slight enhancement of the responses to strong (OVA, Q4R7) agonists (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Upon stimulation with OVA, but not altered peptides, the TCR is quickly downregulated due to its phosphorylation and retention in intracellular vesicles.
source: Upon stimulation with OVA, but not altered peptides, the TCR is quickly downregulated due to its phosphorylation and retention in intracellular vesicles (Cai et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cai et al., 1997.

claim: Csk inhibition alone induced some ligand-independent TCR downregulation.
source: Csk inhibition alone induced some ligand-independent TCR downregulation, but additional downregulation was observed with all peptides, even the weakest G4, which argues for altered signaling of low-affinity peptides at a very upstream step (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Additional TCR downregulation was observed with all peptides, even the weakest G4.
source: Csk inhibition alone induced some ligand-independent TCR downregulation, but additional downregulation was observed with all peptides, even the weakest G4, which argues for altered signaling of low-affinity peptides at a very upstream step (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The null agonist VSV-loaded APCs did not induce similar activation or TCR downregulation.
source: Importantly, the null agonist VSV-loaded APCs did not induce similar activation or TCR downregulation, demonstrating that Csk inhibition works strictly in synergy with a cognate TCR ligand.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Csk inhibition works strictly in synergy with a cognate TCR ligand.
source: Importantly, the null agonist VSV-loaded APCs did not induce similar activation or TCR downregulation, demonstrating that Csk inhibition works strictly in synergy with a cognate TCR ligand.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dose-dependent enhancement of signaling was observed at 100–1000 nM 3-IB-PP1 for weak agonists Q4H7 and G4.
source: Surprisingly we observed dose-dependent enhancement of signaling at 100–1000 nM 3-IB-PP1, where increased Lck pY394 was weakly detectable and at most 50% above the basal level.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: At 100–1000 nM 3-IB-PP1, increased Lck pY394 was weakly detectable and at most 50% above the basal level.
source: Surprisingly we observed dose-dependent enhancement of signaling at 100–1000 nM 3-IB-PP1, where increased Lck pY394 was weakly detectable and at most 50% above the basal level.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3A and 4B.

claim: Relatively weak Lck hyperactivation was sufficient to enhance the recognition of weak agonists.
source: Thus, relatively weak Lck hyperactivation was sufficient to enhance the recognition of weak agonists.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data shown in Figures 3A and 4B.

claim: There are Csk-independent mechanisms for sensing agonist dose.
source: The lower plateau suggests that there are Csk-independent mechanisms for sensing agonist dose.
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The EC50 concentration of Csk inhibition for CD69 upregulation was dependent on agonist quality and dose.
source: Remarkably, the EC50 concentration of Csk inhibition for CD69 upregulation was still dependent on agonist quality and dose (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: At a lower agonist dose, the weaker peptide G4 required double the amount of 3-IB-PP1 than Q4H7.
source: At a lower agonist dose, the weaker peptide G4 required double the amount of 3-IB-PP1 than Q4H7.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Csk inhibition fine-tunes the response to agonist dose and affinity sensing in peripheral T cells.
source: These observations argue that Csk inhibition fine-tunes the response to agonist dose and affinity sensing in peripheral T cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: A substantial amount of active Lck is present in the basal state and does not change with TCR ligation.
source: Since a substantial amount of active Lck is present in the basal state and does not change with TCR ligation, it has been hypothesized that the pre-existing pool of active Lck is responsible for the highly sensitive and rapid initiation of TCR signaling in response to ligand engagement (Nika et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nika et al., 2010.

claim: The pre-existing pool of active Lck is responsible for the highly sensitive and rapid initiation of TCR signaling in response to ligand engagement.
source: Since a substantial amount of active Lck is present in the basal state and does not change with TCR ligation, it has been hypothesized that the pre-existing pool of active Lck is responsible for the highly sensitive and rapid initiation of TCR signaling in response to ligand engagement (Nika et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nika et al., 2010.

claim: By controlling the amount of active Lck present, Csk regulates the responsiveness of the T cell to receptor stimulus.
source: Hence, a likely explanation for our observations is that by controlling the amount of active Lck present, Csk regulates the responsiveness of the T cell to receptor stimulus.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and previous knowledge.

claim: The size of the active pool of Lck is especially critical for affinity discrimination of different agonistic peptides.
source: Our data supports the model that the size of the active pool of Lck is especially critical for affinity discrimination of different agonistic peptides.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: Strong agonists have a long half-life of pMHC-TCR and have sufficient time to recruit active Lck and initiate downstream events.
source: Strong agonists have a long half-life of pMHC-TCR and have sufficient time to recruit active Lck and initiate downstream events, while weak agonists with short half-lives are most sensitive to the availability of active Lck before the pMHC-TCR complex falls apart.
evidence: This is stated as part of the kinetic proofreading model.

claim: Weak agonists with short half-lives are most sensitive to the availability of active Lck before the pMHC-TCR complex falls apart.
source: Strong agonists have a long half-life of pMHC-TCR and have sufficient time to recruit active Lck and initiate downstream events, while weak agonists with short half-lives are most sensitive to the availability of active Lck before the pMHC-TCR complex falls apart.
evidence: This is stated as part of the kinetic proofreading model.

claim: The different amounts of Lck loaded on the CD4 and CD8 co-receptors can explain the different half-life range of positively and negatively selecting ligands for CD4 and CD8 cells.
source: The different amounts of Lck loaded on the CD4 and CD8 co-receptors can explain the different half-life range of positively and negatively selecting ligands for CD4 and CD8 cells (Stepanek et al., 2014); however, this is a genetically established parameter.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stepanek et al., 2014.

claim: Recruitment of active Lck is critical for affinity discrimination.
source: Our data supports the model that recruitment of active Lck is critical for affinity discrimination, but offers an alternative mechanism for its regulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: By controlling the fraction of active Lck, Csk can modulate the activation threshold and affinity discrimination of T cells.
source: By controlling the fraction of active Lck, Csk can also modulate the activation threshold and affinity discrimination of T cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Csk localization and activity is dynamically controlled by phosphorylation-dependent recruitment to transmembrane and cytoplasmic adaptors.
source: Notably, since Csk localization and activity is dynamically controlled by phosphorylation-dependent recruitment to transmembrane and cytoplasmic adaptors, this could enable flexibility in affinity recognition in different settings.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Csk has been found to be differentially localized in naive and antigen-experienced T cells.
source: For example, Csk has been found to be differentially localized in naive and antigen-experienced T cells (Borger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Borger et al., 2013.

claim: The adaptor molecule Themis was characterized as critical for the suppression of weak agonists in thymocytes.
source: Recently, the adaptor molecule Themis was characterized as critical for the suppression of weak agonists in thymocytes, while PTPN22 serves a similar role in in effector cells (Fu et al., 2013; Salmond et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fu et al., 2013 and Salmond et al., 2014.

claim: PTPN22 serves a similar role to Themis in effector cells.
source: Recently, the adaptor molecule Themis was characterized as critical for the suppression of weak agonists in thymocytes, while PTPN22 serves a similar role in in effector cells (Fu et al., 2013; Salmond et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fu et al., 2013 and Salmond et al., 2014.

claim: Csk, via its regulation of Lck, regulates naive T cell priming to agonists of different potency.
source: Here, we show that Csk, via its regulation of Lck, regulates naive T cell priming to agonists of different potency.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Even very small changes in Lck activity, caused by CskAS inhibition at 200 nM 3-IB-PP1, led to relatively large pY394 changes in the setting of small changes in pY505.
source: Surprisingly, even very small changes in Lck activity, caused by CskAS inhibition at 200 nM 3-IB-PP1, led to relatively large pY394 changes in the setting of small changes in pY505.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: A small reduction in pY505 induced by low levels of Csk inhibition could lead to autoactivation of a large pool of Lck.
source: Since Y394 phosphorylation is the result of trans-autophosphorylation, it seems likely that a small reduction in pY505 induced by low levels of Csk inhibition, could lead to autoactivation of a large pool of Lck.
evidence: This is an inference from the data and the known mechanism of Lck activation.

claim: A larger pool of active Lck could show strong synergy with the TCR stimulus.
source: Such a larger pool of active Lck could then show strong synergy with the TCR stimulus and is sufficient to markedly enhance the response to very weak agonists.
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: The synergy between TCR stimulus and Csk inhibition had its greatest impact on the activation of downstream signaling molecules.
source: The synergy we observed between TCR stimulus and Csk inhibition, strikingly, had its greatest impact on the activation of downstream signaling molecules.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The synergy is most likely due to positive feedback/signal amplification along the pathway.
source: This is most likely due to positive feedback/signal amplification along the pathway.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed synergy.

claim: Small changes in Lck activity do not as effectively engage negative feedback mechanisms.
source: It is possible that, although small changes in Lck activity greatly sensitize the TCR to weak agonists, such small changes do not as effectively engage negative feedback mechanisms.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed data.

claim: Loss of Csk from the cell membrane has been proposed to lead to TCR signal initiation via activation of Lck.
source: Loss of Csk from the cell membrane, or biochemically defined lipid raft fractions has been proposed to lead to TCR signal initiation via activation of Lck (Torgersen et al., 2001; Davidson et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Torgersen et al., 2001 and Davidson et al., 2003.

claim: This model is contradicted by the lack of appreciable change in Lck phosphorylation upon TCR stimulation.
source: This model is contradicted by the lack of appreciable change in Lck phosphorylation upon TCR stimulation and by unaltered signaling in cells deficient in the lipid-raft-resident Csk adapter PAG (Dobenecker et al., 2005; Xu et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dobenecker et al., 2005 and Xu et al., 2005.

claim: Acute activation of Lck, via weak or strong Csk inhibition, does not lead to full TCR signaling.
source: Our data demonstrate that acute activation of Lck, via weak or strong Csk inhibition, does not lead to full TCR signaling.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Strong Csk inhibition in mature T cells leads to small amounts of phosphorylation of downstream targets like ZAP-70 and PLC-γ1, but not ERK activation or long-term proliferation in the absence of TCR engagement.
source: Strong Csk inhibition in mature T cells leads to small amounts of phosphorylation of downstream targets like ZAP-70 and PLC-γ1, but not ERK activation or long-term proliferation in the absence of TCR engagement.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Lck activation alone is insufficient to trigger complete TCR signaling.
source: Thus, Lck activation alone is insufficient to trigger complete TCR signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: When combined with cognate TCR ligands, very small amounts of Csk inhibition and resultant larger amounts of Lck activation synergize to enhance early biochemical events and downstream activation.
source: However, when combined with cognate TCR ligands, very small amounts of Csk inhibition and resultant larger amounts of Lck activation, synergize to enhance early biochemical events and downstream activation.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1, 2, 3, and 4.

claim: During physiological TCR stimulation, localization of only a small number of Csk molecules is altered and leads to the activation of a small fraction of Lck molecules.
source: Therefore, it is possible that during physiological TCR stimulation, localization of only a small number of Csk molecules is altered and leads to the activation of a small fraction of Lck molecules that would be difficult to detect with current biochemical or imaging methods (Paster et al., 2009; Nika et al., 2010) but might be sufficient to influence downstream signaling.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data and supported by citations to Paster et al., 2009 and Nika et al., 2010.

claim: TCR signal downregulation in the absence of Csk activity is delayed but not abolished.
source: Using acute inhibition of Csk concurrently with TCR stimulation, we were able to follow TCR signal downregulation in the absence of Csk activity and observed that it is delayed but not abolished.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Other molecules are involved in signal termination more prominently than Csk.
source: Our data suggest that other molecules are involved in signal termination more prominently than Csk.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Manipulation of Csk activity by small molecule inhibitors could be useful therapeutically in pathologic settings where suppression or augmentation of T cell responses to antigen is desirable.
source: Such manipulation of Csk activity by small molecule inhibitors could be useful therapeutically, for example in pathologic settings where suppression (i.e., autoimmunity) or augmentation (i.e., vaccines or cancer) of T cell responses to antigen is desirable.
evidence: This is speculation about potential therapeutic applications.

claim: Mice used for these studies were 6–12 weeks of age.
source: Mice used for these studies were 6–12 weeks of age.
evidence: This is a methodological detail.

claim: All mice were housed in a specific pathogen-free facility at UCSF according to the University Animal Care Committee and National Institutes of Health (NIH) guidelines.
source: All mice were housed in a specific pathogen-free facility at UCSF according to the University Animal Care Committee and National Institutes of Health (NIH) guidelines.
evidence: This is a methodological detail.
